title: Slow Motion
narrative: Use it when a second already contains a scene: a fall, a look that decides, a hit whose mechanics matter. Stretching the instant can turn it into dread, grief, or inspection.
Sound is half the meaning. Stretched diegetic noise makes the world heavy.
Real-time audio against slow picture can feel like a memory or a lie. It is the wrong tool when the beat needs speed, comic timing, or spatial inspection of a frozen pose.
If the camera orbits a nearly stopped body, you wanted bullet time. If frames are duplicated and smeared, you wanted step printing.
Do not slow every punch or the rate stops meaning anything.
how: Capture at a higher frame rate than playback and keep a planned shutter (often 180 degrees, so 120 fps is about 1/240 s per frame). You need more light because each exposure is shorter.
Keep gravity, contacts, and anatomy continuous through the extra samples. For generated footage, ask for real intermediate motion, not interpolated mush.
Prompt: Slow motion of [Subject] at 120 to 240 fps playback, dust hanging, fabric delayed, continuous gravity.
when: Use it on a decisive instant a normal rate would hide, such as a glass leaving a waiter's hand. Do not use it as a default look for an entire fight.
vs: Constant slow motion is not a Speed Ramp , which changes rate inside the shot and then recovers. It is not Step Printing , which duplicates low-rate, long-exposure frames into a stuttered lyric smear.
It is not Bullet Time , which decouples a traveling viewpoint from near-frozen action. Freeze Frame stops sampling altogether.
Fast Motion and Time-Lapse crush duration instead of stretching it.
examples_film: Seven Samurai stretches the kidnapper's fall so the death occupies more than its wall-clock instant. The Wild Bunch fragments gunfights through varied slow-motion views so violence becomes duration.
The Matrix is often filed here, but the rooftop lean is closer to bullet time. In the Mood for Love belongs with step printing more than with clean overcranked silk.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Bullet Time or a freeze. The tell is a stopped body with a moving camera, or a still with no new frames of motion.
Fix: keep the subject traveling through the action, keep anatomy and gravity continuous, and specify 120 to 240 fps playback rather than an orbit around a sculpture.

faq.q: What is Slow Motion in film?
faq.a: Slow motion is overcranked or retimed footage that occupies more screen time than the event took to happen, so small physical details become readable.

faq.q: Slow Motion vs Bullet Time
faq.a: Slow motion stretches the subject's action while the camera may stay simple. Bullet time nearly freezes the action while the viewpoint travels around it.

faq.q: When should I use Slow Motion?
faq.a: When one second already contains the scene: a fall, a look, or an impact whose mechanics or grief need extra duration.

faq.q: How do I prompt Slow Motion for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write 120 to 240 fps playback, delayed fabric, hanging particles, and continuous anatomy. Forbid a frozen subject with an orbiting camera.

title: Speed Ramp
narrative: Treat it as temporal close-up. The shot walks up in real time, lands on the fact that matters, and releases.
A fight, a catch, a look across a room can all take the ramp if the event is readable. The audience should feel one continuous action, not a new clip glued on.
It is the wrong tool when the whole beat should stay slow, or when you only need a smash of magnification. If rate never returns, you shot slow motion and called it a ramp.
If the picture punches in by focal length, you wanted a crash zoom. Do not ramp to hide unreadable choreography.
how: Capture enough temporal detail (high frame rate) that both the fast and slow portions have samples. Identify the motivated event, then shape the acceleration curve and matching motion blur.
The body must stay mechanically continuous through the change. Prompt: Speed ramp on [Subject], real time slamming into slow motion at the impact or glance, then releasing.
when: Use it to mark one instant inside a fight or a look, such as a board leaving the ramp at the peak of a jump. Do not use it on every cut or the emphasis dies.
vs: A ramp is not constant Slow Motion , which never returns to real time. It is not a Crash Zoom In , which changes focal length rather than the clock.
Freeze Frame holds one image. Bullet Time lets the camera orbit a nearly stopped instant instead of stretching and releasing the same viewpoint's action.
examples_film: 300 moves combat between fast and extended slow-motion beats so selected blows become readable. Sherlock Holmes (2009) isolates anticipated fight details, then snaps back to the hit as performed.
The Matrix mixes rates around chosen impacts, though its array orbits are a different machine.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is wall-to-wall Slow Motion . The tell is a shot that never returns to real time, or a jump in pose at the speed change.
Fix: write approach, hold, and release, and keep the body continuous through the curve.

faq.q: What is Speed Ramp in film?
faq.a: A speed ramp is a change of playback or capture speed inside one shot, used to emphasize a single instant and then return.

faq.q: Speed Ramp vs Slow Motion
faq.a: Slow motion holds one stretched rate. A speed ramp enters that rate at a motivated event and leaves it, so approach and recovery stay fast.

faq.q: When should I use Speed Ramp?
faq.a: When one contact, recognition, or turn must be inspected without draining the energy of the surrounding action.

faq.q: How do I prompt Speed Ramp for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write real time into slow motion at a named beat, then recovery. Demand one continuous action and matching motion blur, not a cut to a different clip.

title: Step Printing
narrative: Use it for longing that cannot move at normal speed: a walk through rain, a pursuit that feels remembered, a figure isolated from a city's rush. The smear belongs inside the frame.
The step belongs between frames. Together they make memory feel unstable without a digital glitch overlay.
It is the wrong tool for a readable impact study, a fight that must stay mechanical, or anxiety that should skip like a damaged mind. Those are slow motion and stutter.
Do not interpolate the cadence away. If the walk becomes silk, you left the technique.
how: Shoot or generate a low temporal sample (often well below 24 fps) with enough shutter time for motion blur, then duplicate frames to the delivery rate. Test the cadence.

Keep practical lights saturated and the lonely figure more readable than the crowd. Prompt: Step-printed motion of [Subject], frames duplicated, stuttering lyric delay, long-exposure smear inside each frame.
when: Use it on a rain walk or a night counter where one person should separate from the city's rush. Do not use it when you need clean 120 fps anatomy of a hit.
vs: Step printing is not silk Slow Motion , which samples densely and interpolates smoothly. It is not Stutter / Stop-Stutter , which drops or repeats frames as anxious rhythm without requiring long-exposure smear.
Motion Blur can exist at normal cadence. Stop Motion builds poses by hand between exposures rather than reprinting live action.
examples_film: Chungking Express gives crowded street movement a blurred, stuttering temporal texture. Fallen Angels uses irregular urban motion and smear as a lonely gait.
In the Mood for Love is often remembered as slow romance. Much of that delay is step-printed texture rather than overcranked silk.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Slow Motion . The tell is clean high-frame-rate motion with no step and no smear, or a datamosh overlay.
Fix: specify low-rate capture, long shutter, duplicated frames, and a cadence you can count.

faq.q: What is Step Printing in film?
faq.a: Step printing repeats or skips frames, often after low-rate long-exposure capture, so motion smears inside frames and advances in steps.

faq.q: Step Printing vs Slow Motion
faq.a: Slow motion is dense temporal sampling played slowly and smoothly. Step printing is a stepped, smeared cadence made by reprinting frames.

faq.q: When should I use Step Printing?
faq.a: When a walk, a pursuit, or a night street should feel like delayed memory rather than inspected physics.

faq.q: How do I prompt Step Printing for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write duplicated frames, stuttering lyric delay, and long-exposure smear. Forbid smooth 120 fps slow motion and generic digital glitches.

title: Stop Motion
narrative: Use it when motion should feel made: puppets, replacement faces, dinosaurs that are sculptures, a fox whose fur is fabric. Weight, texture, and small irregularities are the performance.
Live-action smoothness would be the wrong world. It is the wrong tool for a choppy filter on a real actor, or for step-printed streets.
If the fox's fur flows like photographed animal hair, you left the craft. A generated 'stop-motion look' is an aesthetic.
Frame-by-frame production is a method. Say which one you want.
how: Lock the camera. Repeat the lighting.
Plan pose spacing. Secure the model so it does not drift.
Replacement animation swaps parts (mouths, lids) between frames. For generated approximations, specify consistent materials, visible joints, and deliberate increments.
Prompt: Stop-motion of [Subject], stepped poses, tactile increment, time built by hand.
when: Use it when a puppet or object should perform as a photographed sculpture, such as a fox folding paper on a miniature desk. Do not use it as a jitter preset on live action.
vs: Stop motion is not Step Printing of live footage. It is a branch of Animation , specifically frame-by-frame object animation, including replacement animation.
Stutter / Stop-Stutter skip-frames living time. Low Shutter makes live action staccato without posing a model.
examples_film: King Kong (1933) animates Kong and prehistoric creatures as physical models. Jason and the Argonauts combines Harryhausen figures with live action in the skeleton fight.
The Nightmare Before Christmas and Coraline perform with puppets and miniatures. Fantastic Mr.
Fox keeps tactile fur and handmade increment as the world's law.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a live-action jitter or Step Printing . The tell is morphing materials, melting paper, or continuously flowing hair.
Fix: consistent model, deliberate pose changes, locked camera, repeatable light.

faq.q: What is Stop Motion in film?
faq.a: Stop motion is frame-by-frame photography of adjusted objects or puppets, so their successive poses create movement.

faq.q: Stop Motion vs Step Printing
faq.a: Step printing reprints live-action frames into a smear-and-step cadence. Stop motion builds each frame by moving a physical (or consistent digital) model.

faq.q: When should I use Stop Motion?
faq.a: When the world should feel handmade: puppets, miniatures, objects that perform. Not when you only want live action to hitch.

faq.q: How do I prompt Stop Motion for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write stepped poses, tactile materials, pose-to-pose cadence, and a stable camera. Forbid fluid live-action motion and choppy-filter shortcuts.

title: Stutter / Stop-Stutter
narrative: Use it when thought itself is damaged: obsession, panic, a headache that cuts time into chips. The picture may stay in the same setup while frames go missing or repeat.
Cadence is the meaning. A little is a twitch.
A lot is a seizure. It is the wrong tool for Wong Kar-wai rain, for Godard-style discontinuous geography, or for stop-motion craft.
If the smear is romantic, you wanted step printing. If the camera angle or body position jumps, you wanted a jump cut.
Do not add a codec glitch unless the story is a broken file.
how: Start from a clean take, then remove or duplicate frames on a planned irregular grid. You can also skip in camera by lowering sample rate without long-exposure smear.
Keep identity and space continuous so the hitch reads as time, not as a cut. Prompt: Stuttered motion of [Subject], frames dropping or repeating, a glitch in time, anxiety as rhythm.
when: Use it when a thought or a panic attack should skip, such as a close face whose blinks do not land on a steady clock. Do not use it as lyric street texture.
vs: Stutter is not Step Printing , which reprints long-exposure frames into a smeared delay. It is not a Jump Cut , which discards time and often shows a spatial jump in the same setup.
Stop Motion is pose-to-pose craft. Datamosh is compression damage.
Keep them separate in the prompt.
examples_film: Pi uses staccato, high-contrast skipping so numbers and pain share a rhythm. Music videos often stutter a gesture as a beat.
Aronofsky's later montage grammar (Requiem among them) neighbors this hitch without being identical to skip-frame stutter.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Step Printing or Jump Cut . The tell is romantic long-exposure crowds, or a sudden change of body position that reads as an edit.
Fix: keep space continuous and make the cadence irregular. Count the missing frames.

faq.q: What is Stutter / Stop-Stutter in film?
faq.a: Stutter is playback that drops or repeats frames so time hitches. The setup usually stays put while the clock skips.

faq.q: Stutter vs Step Printing
faq.a: Step printing is smeared, lyric, duplicated-frame delay. Stutter is anxious skip-or-repeat rhythm without requiring long-exposure texture.

faq.q: When should I use Stutter?
faq.a: When panic, obsession, or pain should make the mind skip. Keep the same setup so the hitch is temporal.

faq.q: How do I prompt Stutter for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write frames repeating and skipping, anxious rhythm, same camera setup. Forbid smooth slow motion, romantic smear, and jump-cut geography.

title: Time-Lapse
narrative: Use it to reveal a pattern no one can stand still long enough to see. Weather, construction, traffic, a plant, a city emptying and filling.
People often stop being protagonists and become a system. The camera is usually locked so the only motion is time.

It is the wrong tool for a comic undercrank of a performance, or for a still hero in a racing crowd (that is a different recipe). If the camera must walk the street while hours collapse, you wanted a hyperlapse.
Do not call a fast crowd under a stuck sun a full day-to-night lapse.
how: Plan interval, total duration, exposure, and stability. A locked head is the default.
For day-to-night, ramp exposure so windows light as the sky dies. The sun and shadows must travel if the claim is a full day.
Prompt: Time-lapse of [Subject] or the world around them, hours in seconds, shadows sweeping, crowds as smoke.
when: Use it to show weather, construction, or a night becoming morning from a stable viewpoint. Do not use it to make an actor's performance merely faster.
vs: Time-lapse is not Fast Motion , which accelerates a continuous take. Hyperlapse adds significant camera travel through space on top of the interval.
Timelapse Landscape is the weather-and-shadow specialty. Timelapse Human freezes one will inside a racing crowd.
Timelapse Glam interval-samples wardrobe on a held face.
examples_film: Koyaanisqatsi turns traffic, crowds, and urban cycles into large-scale patterns. Baraka organizes cities and ritual through altered temporal scales.
Both are grammar for interval sampling, not frames to copy.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Fast Motion . The tell is smeared pedestrians under a sun that never moves, or architecture that morphs.
Fix: write hours in seconds, a stable camera, and continuous shadow travel. If only people race, you have not shown a day.

faq.q: What is Time-Lapse in film?
faq.a: Time-lapse is interval photography: widely spaced frames played continuously so slow processes occupy a short passage.

faq.q: Time-Lapse vs Fast Motion
faq.a: Fast motion speeds a continuous recording. Time-lapse skips long stretches between frames, which is how a day, a build, or a sky can play in seconds.

faq.q: When should I use Time-Lapse?
faq.a: When the story is a process too slow for real time: weather, construction, crowds as flow, night becoming morning.

faq.q: How do I prompt Time-Lapse for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write hours in seconds, sweeping shadows, and a stable viewpoint. Require the sun to move if you claim a full day. Do not only speed a crowd.

title: Timelapse Glam
narrative: Use it to show transformation as labor rather than as a cut to a new costume. Stylists swarm.
Hangers fly. Identity must survive the swarm or the face becomes a morph.
The camera is usually locked. The clock is the dressing room's, not the street's.
It is the wrong tool for landscape days, racing crowds, or a freeze of the world. If the city is the process, you wanted time-lapse or timelapse landscape.
If only the person is a statue in traffic, you wanted timelapse human. Do not let the skull drift.
how: Lock identity, eyeline, and camera. Interval-sample while wardrobe and hair change in discrete, readable steps.
Hands of stylists may smear. The face should not.
Prompt: Timelapse glam of [Subject], styling swarm, clothes and hair changing while the face holds.
when: Use it when a look is assembled in public, such as a held face while stylists swap dresses at interval speed. Do not use it to time-lapse a skyline.
vs: This is a specialty of Time-Lapse , not a Glam lighting pattern alone. Timelapse Human holds a person while a crowd races.
Timelapse Landscape holds geography while weather races. A montage of costume changes with cuts is editing, not interval sampling.
examples_film: Vogue transformation films and fashion-week process pieces are the native grammar. Music videos use interval wardrobe bursts on a held star.
Feature films more often cut montages. If you need a narrative cousin, think process, not a copied title sequence.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a costume Montage or a face morph. The tell is a changing skull, or a city time-lapse with no styling work.
Fix: hold identity and camera, interval the wardrobe, keep stylist hands as the swarm.

faq.q: What is Timelapse Glam in film?
faq.a: Timelapse glam interval-samples a styling session so clothes and hair change quickly while the face remains a stable identity.

faq.q: Timelapse Glam vs Time-Lapse
faq.a: Time-lapse is the parent interval method. Timelapse glam restricts it to a held person whose wardrobe and hair are the changing weather.

faq.q: When should I use Timelapse Glam?
faq.a: When transformation is the beat and should be seen as process: a look assembled, not a cut to a new costume.

faq.q: How do I prompt Timelapse Glam for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write a still face, a styling swarm, and clothes changing at high speed. Lock identity. Forbid morphing skulls and city-only lapses.

title: Timelapse Human
narrative: Use it when isolation is a rate difference: the subject decides, waits, or grieves at 24 fps while the city is hours. Commuters become flow.
The camera is usually locked so the contrast stays readable. A tiny sway in the hero is allowed.

Walking at full speed through a lapse crowd breaks the contract. It is the wrong tool when the world should freeze and the hero should walk (frozen in motion), or when weather is the subject (timelapse landscape).
The Matrix lobby is often misfiled here. That lobby is bullet time: an orbit around a crushed instant, not interval crowds around a statue.
how: Lock the hero's mark and the camera. Sample passersby at long intervals, or composite a held performance over a crowd lapse.
Shadows on the hero should not travel like a full day unless that is the story. Prompt: Timelapse human of [Subject] frozen in a rushing crowd, people as smoke, one still will.
when: Use it when one person should hold a station or a square while the crowd becomes smoke. Do not use it when that person must walk through a stopped city.
vs: This is Time-Lapse applied to extras around a held lead. Frozen in Motion freezes the crowd and lets the lead (or camera) move.
Bullet Time orbits a near-frozen event. Timelapse Landscape races weather, not pedestrians.
Fast Motion would accelerate the hero too.
examples_film: Koyaanisqatsi turns crowds into systems. The still-person-in-racing-crowd recipe is a commercial and music-video cousin of that grammar.
The Matrix lobby stills are a frequent false reference. They belong with bullet time.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Frozen in Motion or Bullet Time . The tell is stopped extras and a walking hero, or a camera orbit around hanging brass.
Fix: subject holds, crowd races, camera locked, people as smoke.

faq.q: What is Timelapse Human in film?
faq.a: Timelapse human keeps one person nearly still while interval-sampled crowds race around them, so isolation reads as a difference in clocks.

faq.q: Timelapse Human vs Frozen in Motion
faq.a: Timelapse human races the world around a held person. Frozen in motion stops the world so a chosen person or the camera can still move.

faq.q: When should I use Timelapse Human?
faq.a: When one will should stand while a station, lobby, or street becomes flow. The hero is the still axis.

faq.q: How do I prompt Timelapse Human for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write crowds time-lapsing around a still [Subject], people as smoke, camera locked. Forbid a walking hero in a frozen crowd and bullet-time orbits.

title: Timelapse Landscape
narrative: Use it when the story is a sky, a desert, a city grid as climate, a ridge that must survive several suns. The camera is locked or on a slow, even move that does not fight the sun's path.
Buildings and rock stay solid. Clouds are the motion.
It is the wrong tool for wardrobe process, a still hero in a smoking crowd, or undercranked acting. If the camera walks the avenue in steps, you wanted a hyperlapse.
If only headlights streak under a stuck sun, you have not shown a landscape day.
how: Choose interval from the process (clouds faster than a shadow-day, stars slower). Lock off or use a motion-control pan.
Ramp exposure for day-to-night. Keep the sun's arc continuous.
Prompt: Timelapse landscape around [Subject] or their place, clouds and shadows sweeping, hours in seconds.
when: Use it to show the day turning over a ridge, a square, or a citadel. Do not use it as a crowd recipe with a motionless sky.
vs: This is Time-Lapse aimed at weather and terrain. Aerial may carry it if the viewpoint is high, but height is not the interval.
Hyperlapse moves the camera through space in steps. Timelapse Human races people.
Fast Motion speeds a continuous take.
examples_film: Baraka and Koyaanisqatsi are the landscape-and-city interval grammar: clouds, shadows, and human systems at non-human rates. Later nature films inherit the same sun-and-cloud contract.
The still should imply a phase of day, not a morphing mountain.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Fast Motion or Timelapse Human . The tell is racing people under a stuck sun, or mountains that melt.
Fix: hours in seconds, traveling shadows, solid ground, camera stable or slowly authored.

faq.q: What is Timelapse Landscape in film?
faq.a: Timelapse landscape is interval photography of a place so weather, shadows, and sun travel occupy a short passage.

faq.q: Timelapse Landscape vs Time-Lapse
faq.a: Time-lapse is the method. Timelapse landscape restricts the subject to geography and climate, not wardrobe or a held pedestrian.

faq.q: When should I use Timelapse Landscape?
faq.a: When the day turning is the beat: clouds, shadows, night becoming morning over a stable place.

faq.q: How do I prompt Timelapse Landscape for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write hours in seconds, sweeping clouds and shadows, and solid geography. Require the sun to move. Do not only speed a crowd.

title: 3D Render
narrative: Fashion that wants to be a toy, ads, a character who is not quite flesh: studio HDRI, turntable still, no film grain unless you are hybridizing on purpose. A period drama usually dies here.
The library cousin is motion capture into an invented body, where attention and hesitation matter more than spectacle. The named look on the page is the computed surface.
Do not confuse a photograph labeled CGI with this. If pores and grain survive, you still shot a camera.
how: Lock a studio camera, 50mm to 85mm, eye height or a slight turntable three-quarter. HDRI wrap, subsurface that is slightly too even, infinite cyc, perfect contacts.
No grain, no dirty anamorphic. Prompt: 3D-render look of [Subject], CG shader, clean GI, a person as a product visualization.
when: A product-person still, an ad, a character who should not quite be flesh. Do not use it on a period drama unless the point is that they are computed.
vs: Photogrammetry is a scan of real surfaces, dirt and all. Product is the lighting and turntable discipline for objects.
3D render applies that computed wrap to a person. Action Figure is polymer toy matter, not shader skin.
Marble is geology, not GI.
examples_film: TRON: Legacy's clean CG bodies, The Congress , and the invented-body work in The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers , Rise of the Planet of the Apes , and Avatar . Borrow computed light and a stable model, not a still.
Capture is not a finished performance if you are doing the mocap cousin.
mistakes: A photograph with CGI in the prompt that still has pores and grain, or a slide into Photogrammetry dirt. The tell is photochemical noise.
Fix it: shader wrap, clean GI, cyc, computed skin.

faq.q: What is 3D Render in film?
faq.a: A computed-surface look: clean GI, shader skin, product-visualization light on a person. Related pipelines include motion capture into an invented body, which still needs animation judgment.

faq.q: 3D Render vs Photogrammetry
faq.a: Photogrammetry captures real surfaces, including dirt. 3D render is shader and GI, too clean on purpose. If you can see scanned grime, you wanted photogrammetry.

faq.q: When should I use 3D Render?
faq.a: Ads, toy-fashion, a character who is not quite flesh. Skip period realism unless the computation is the point.

faq.q: How do I prompt 3D Render for AI image or video?
faq.a: Studio HDRI, no grain, then: 3D-render look of [Subject], CG shader, clean GI, a person as a product visualization. Demand infinite cyc and too-perfect skin.

title: 2000s Paparazzi
narrative: Scandal, youth, a character hunted by attention: club rope, sidewalk, car door, night. Motion smear is allowed.
Beauty light is not. Superstar is the sanctioned cousin.
Magazine is the page. This is the accident you keep.
It is the wrong tool for a royal portrait, a beauty cover, or a planned fashion key. If the red-eye and the wall-shadow are gone, you shot glam.
how: Chest to eye height, 28mm to 50mm, as if a compact in a crowd. Direct on-camera flash, hard shadow on a wall, compact-camera artifacts, sidewalk or club rope.
Do not beauty-light the face. No masthead.
Prompt: 2000s paparazzi of [Subject], on-camera flash, compact digital, sidewalk fame, a decade of glare.
when: A hunted exit, a scandal still, youth under theft-light. Do not use it for a sanctioned cover or a beauty dish.
vs: Superstar is consent and cover light. Flash Cut is an edit of white frames.
2000s paparazzi is the still of that theft: compact digital, on-camera flash, face not posed. Glam is the opposite discipline.
examples_film: The Bling Ring lives in sidewalk fame and ugly flash. Paparazzi (2004) treats the compact strobe as a weapon.
A thousand club-exit stills are the grammar. The frame should look accidental.
mistakes: Soft flash that still looks like fashion, or a slide into Superstar . The tell is no wall-shadow and no compact artifact.
Fix it: on-camera flash, ugly, accidental, face not ready.

faq.q: What is 2000s Paparazzi in film?
faq.a: A theft-light recipe: on-camera flash, compact digital, sidewalk glare, a face not ready. It is a lamp and a sensor, not a camera move.

faq.q: 2000s Paparazzi vs Superstar
faq.a: Superstar is sanctioned beauty and a room already looking. 2000s paparazzi is stolen strobe. If the person looks ready and rich in the light, you wanted superstar.

faq.q: When should I use 2000s Paparazzi?
faq.a: Scandal, hunted exits, youth under attention. Skip royal portraits and beauty covers.

faq.q: How do I prompt 2000s Paparazzi for AI image or video?
faq.a: Compact flash, sidewalk, then: 2000s paparazzi of [Subject], on-camera flash, compact digital, sidewalk fame, a decade of glare. Keep the wall-shadow. Do not beauty-light.

title: Acid
narrative: Nights that went wrong, posters, a memory that chemically failed: a face still held, edges melting, magentas and yellows overcooked. LSD is wet perception.
Acid is the print after the sun. Cross-process is a cousin in the soup.
It is the wrong tool for grocery-store realism, and the wrong tool if you add trails. Trails belong to LSD.
If it looks festive rather than damaged, you shot a party filter.
how: Lock off, 35mm to 50mm, eye height. Keep a readable face.
Prompt melted edges, overcooked magentas and yellows, shifted silver. Do not add trails unless you want LSD as well.
Pick one. Prompt: Acid look on [Subject], burned chroma, melting edges, a print left in the sun too long.
when: A night that chemically failed, a poster, a damaged memory. Do not use it as a rainbow party grade, and do not mix trails unless you mean LSD.
vs: LSD is wet trails and breathing walls. Acid is print damage.
Cross Process is a specific soup mistake that shifts hues. Acid is the named ruin: melt, burn, sun-sick dyes.
Not a festive LUT.
examples_film: Enter the Void can overlap with LSD, but its dye is usable as burned chroma. Spring Breakers cooks color until it hurts.
Chemistry, not a party filter. Grammar, not a frame to copy.
mistakes: A rainbow LUT, or trails from LSD stacked on melt. The tell is festive rather than ruined.
Fix it: show the melt, burn the dyes, hold the face.

faq.q: What is Acid in film?
faq.a: A ruined-print look: burned chroma, melting edges, dyes that sat in the sun. It is chemical damage, not a rainbow grade.

faq.q: Acid vs LSD
faq.a: LSD is wet perception: trails, breathing walls. Acid is a print that failed: melt and burn. Trails belong to LSD. Damage belongs to acid.

faq.q: When should I use Acid?
faq.a: Failed nights, posters, chemically sick memory. Skip grocery realism and party rainbows.

faq.q: How do I prompt Acid for AI image or video?
faq.a: Hold the face, then: Acid look on [Subject], burned chroma, melting edges, a print left in the sun too long. Forbid trails unless you mean LSD instead.

title: Action Figure
narrative: Satire, kid myth, a hero reduced to product: one figure, diorama base, rivets, polymer skin. Mighty fighter is a living sprite.
This is the box. A sincere war story should not become a doll unless that is the point.
It is the wrong tool when you still see pores and cloth weave as fabric. You need plastic.
Joints. Toy scale in the light.
Do not render readable packaging type.
how: Slightly high studio camera, 50mm, lock-off, as if the toy is on a card. Hard product keys, blister shine, visible joints, painted costume.
Diorama base allowed. No letters.
Prompt: Action-figure of [Subject], plastic joints, blister-card lighting, a toy of a person.
when: Satire, kid myth, a hero as SKU. Do not use it on a sincere war story unless the reduction is the sentence.
vs: Mighty Fighter is a living win pose. Diorama is the miniature world under them.
